title: Why Is System Design Interview Important

segments.text: In this short video, we discussed why system design interviews are so important.
System design interviews are a critical part of the hiring process for software engineers,
particularly at top tech companies.
Software is expensive to build.
These companies need experienced engineers with strong system design skills.
This increases their odds of building things right the first time.
And system design interviews are a predominant method to gauge those skills.
System design interviews are a way that much more heavily for senior engineers.
For most well-known companies, staff level positions require multiple rounds of system designs.
This all makes sense.
The more senior we are in software engineering, the more system design matters in a job.
Typically, in another way, how we perform in the system design rounds, greatly impacts
the leveling and compensation decisions.
Now, what do these companies look for in the system design rounds?
And what are some of the dos and dos in these interviews?
The number one signal these company look for is how we approach problem solving
and how we think about designing large scale systems.
They want to see if we can think critically,
make and justify trade-offs between different design options,
while balancing different constraints.
They want to see whether we could communicate our ideas clearly.
They want to see if we could work well with their teams,
but with that in mind, here are some quick tips on dos and dos.
Do understand the problem statement and requirements before designing.
Often the question is deliberately vague.
Do ask clarifying questions.
Don't jump into solution without first understanding the problem.
Do consider multiple designs,
and clearly articulate trade-offs between them.
Do consider scalability, latency, and other non-functional requirements.
The higher the level, the more important are the non-functional aspects of the design.
Don't over engineer or add unnecessary complexity.
Do communicate clearly and explain the reasoning behind our design decisions.
System design interviews are no dos stressful.
This I hope that these short tips would be a good reminder for us all
on how to approach these critical interviews.
In future videos, we'll design some popular distributed systems,
like WhatsApp, Facebook, News Feed, etc.
Stay tuned.
You would like to learn more about system design,
check out our books and weekly newsletter.
Please subscribe if you learned something new.
Thank you so much and we'll see you next time.
